text: A backup copy of the heeyID database leaves the bank, on a disk that nobody should have taken.
prefix: A backup copy of the heeyID database leaves the bank, on a disk that nobody should have taken.

text: On it are the customers of the bank: names, passport data, addresses and phone numbers.
prefix: On it are the customers of the bank: names, passport data, addresses and phone numbers.

text: Aziz is one of them.
prefix: Aziz is one of them.

text: What can the person with the disk read?
prefix: What can the person with the disk read?

text: In Lesson 7, each adapter held a secret, and the platform kept passports encrypted.
prefix: In Lesson 7, each adapter held a secret, and the platform kept passports encrypted.

text: This lesson shows where every key lives, and why the disk is worth so little.
prefix: This lesson shows where every key lives, and why the disk is worth so little.

text: All the keys of heeyID live in Vault, and the Vault belongs to the bank.
prefix: All the keys of heeyID live in Vault, and the Vault belongs to the bank.

text: Each zone has its own new Vault, and the security team of the bank keeps the keys that unseal it.
prefix: Each zone has its own new Vault, and the security team of the bank keeps the keys that unseal it.

text: The vendor never sees one of them.
prefix: The vendor never sees one of them.

text: I think this is the line in the design that matters most: the bank keeps the keys.
prefix: I think this is the line in the design that matters most: the bank keeps the keys.

text: Six kinds of keys sit there.
prefix: Six kinds of keys sit there.

text: Walk across the disk, and meet them one by one.
prefix: Walk across the disk, and meet them one by one.

text: First, the verified identity of Aziz: his names, his document data and his addresses.
prefix: First, the verified identity of Aziz: his names, his document data and his addresses.

text: His record has its own data key, and that data key encrypts the record.
prefix: His record has its own data key, and that data key encrypts the record.

text: The data key is stored next to the record, but wrapped: the installation key-encryption key encrypts it.
prefix: The data key is stored next to the record, but wrapped: the installation key-encryption key encrypts it.

text: The key-encryption key never leaves Vault.
prefix: The key-encryption key never leaves Vault.

text: To read the record, the gateway sends the wrapped data key to Vault, gets it back unwrapped for this one request, and then forgets it.
prefix: To read the record, the gateway sends the wrapped data key to Vault, gets it back unwrapped for this one request, and then forgets it.

text: This is envelope encryption.
prefix: This is envelope encryption.

text: On the disk, the thief has records and wrapped data keys, and no way to open them.
prefix: On the disk, the thief has records and wrapped data keys, and no way to open them.

text: And Vault records each time a key is unwrapped.
prefix: And Vault records each time a key is unwrapped.

text: Second, search.
prefix: Second, search.

text: An operator must find Aziz by his exact personal identification number, among all the rows.
prefix: An operator must find Aziz by his exact personal identification number, among all the rows.

text: But the number is encrypted.
prefix: But the number is encrypted.

text: So the platform keeps a blind index: a keyed hash of the number, made with the installation index key.
prefix: So the platform keeps a blind index: a keyed hash of the number, made with the installation index key.

text: The same number always gives the same index, so an exact search works.
prefix: The same number always gives the same index, so an exact search works.

text: Without the index key, the thief cannot even test a guess.
prefix: Without the index key, the thief cannot even test a guess.

text: The same key makes the digest that binds a session to its device.
prefix: The same key makes the digest that binds a session to its device.

text: Third, the one-time codes.
prefix: Third, the one-time codes.

text: heeyID keeps a code only as a digest, and the digest mixes in a secret pepper from Vault.
prefix: heeyID keeps a code only as a digest, and the digest mixes in a secret pepper from Vault.

text: A short code is easy to guess, so a plain digest of it is easy to reverse.
prefix: A short code is easy to guess, so a plain digest of it is easy to reverse.

text: With the pepper in Vault, the thief cannot even check a guess.
prefix: With the pepper in Vault, the thief cannot even check a guess.

text: Fourth, the audit trail.
prefix: Fourth, the audit trail.

text: Each audit event is chained to the event before it with an HMAC, under the audit key.
prefix: Each audit event is chained to the event before it with an HMAC, under the audit key.

text: Change one event, and the chain breaks.
prefix: Change one event, and the chain breaks.

text: A daily verifier checks the chain, and raises an alert at each break.
prefix: A daily verifier checks the chain, and raises an alert at each break.

text: Fifth, the token signatures.
prefix: Fifth, the token signatures.

text: Keycloak signs each token with the realm keys.
prefix: Keycloak signs each token with the realm keys.

text: They sit in the Keycloak database, encrypted with a secret from Vault.
prefix: They sit in the Keycloak database, encrypted with a secret from Vault.

text: Sixth, the credentials of the outside services: the MyID credential, the TAF client secret, the client certificates of the adapters, and the push credential.
prefix: Sixth, the credentials of the outside services: the MyID credential, the TAF client secret, the client certificates of the adapters, and the push credential.

text: Each credential goes only to the adapter that uses it.
prefix: Each credential goes only to the adapter that uses it.

text: The push credential, for example, arrives as a file for the push adapter, and for nothing else.
prefix: The push credential, for example, arrives as a file for the push adapter, and for nothing else.

text: None of them is ever in the code, on a phone, or in a log.
prefix: None of them is ever in the code, on a phone, or in a log.

text: And the passwords?
prefix: And the passwords?

text: They are not encrypted at all, on purpose.
prefix: They are not encrypted at all, on purpose.

text: heeyID keeps only a slow, salted password hash, and a hash cannot be reversed.
prefix: heeyID keeps only a slow, salted password hash, and a hash cannot be reversed.

text: There is no key to steal, because there is nothing to decrypt.
prefix: There is no key to steal, because there is nothing to decrypt.

text: Keys also age.
prefix: Keys also age.

text: Each key has a rotation period, and the bank sets it.
prefix: Each key has a rotation period, and the bank sets it.

text: When the key-encryption key rotates, its old versions stay for unwrapping, and the platform wraps the data keys again in the background.
prefix: When the key-encryption key rotates, its old versions stay for unwrapping, and the platform wraps the data keys again in the background.

text: Old audit keys stay too, so old chains still verify.
prefix: Old audit keys stay too, so old chains still verify.

text: Each key has an owner who approves its change: the security team of the bank, or its platform team.
prefix: Each key has an owner who approves its change: the security team of the bank, or its platform team.

text: Back to the disk.
prefix: Back to the disk.

text: The thief has encrypted records, wrapped data keys, blind indexes, code digests, password hashes and a signed audit chain.
prefix: The thief has encrypted records, wrapped data keys, blind indexes, code digests, password hashes and a signed audit chain.

text: Every key that could open them stays in the Vault of the bank.
prefix: Every key that could open them stays in the Vault of the bank.

text: The disk is a loss of hardware, not a loss of identities.
prefix: The disk is a loss of hardware, not a loss of identities.

text: To recap: one Vault for each zone, in the bank.
prefix: To recap: one Vault for each zone, in the bank.

text: Six kinds of keys: the key-encryption key, the index key, the code pepper, the audit key, the realm keys, and the credentials of the outside services.
prefix: Six kinds of keys: the key-encryption key, the index key, the code pepper, the audit key, the realm keys, and the credentials of the outside services.

text: Envelope encryption for identities, a blind index for search, and digests for codes and passwords.
prefix: Envelope encryption for identities, a blind index for search, and digests for codes and passwords.

text: The keys never leave the bank, and they never reach a phone.
prefix: The keys never leave the bank, and they never reach a phone.

text: But the apps of the bank still keep something on the phone, and still call heeyID.
prefix: But the apps of the bank still keep something on the phone, and still call heeyID.

text: What may an app keep, and how does it talk to heeyID?
prefix: What may an app keep, and how does it talk to heeyID?
